title: A second app, and a component

# Week 6, Day 1.1 - Prerequisites check

Today you replace twelve near-identical methods with one. That needs two pieces of
TypeScript you have not used yet.

| Concept | Taught in |
|---|---|
| `class`, `constructor`, `readonly` | [week3/day3_1](/learn/w3/d3/p1) |
| `abstract`, `extends`, `super`, `protected` | [week5/day3_1](/learn/w5/d3/p1) |
| **`switch` / `case` / `break` / `default`** | new - below |
| **`throw` and `Error`** | new - below |
| **Union of string literals** | new - below |

**Next:** [Day 1.2 - A second app, and a component](/learn/w6/d1/p2)

## Concept 1 - `switch`

One value, many destinations. An `if/else if` chain does the same job; `switch` reads as a
table, which is what a list of tabs actually is.

| Keyword | Job |
|---|---|
| `case "x":` | run this branch when the value is `"x"` |
| `break` | stop here - **without it execution falls into the next case** |
| `default` | nothing matched |

// Your turn — retype the example above from memory, then run it.
// Typing beats reading. Peek above if you get stuck.

## Concept 2 - the fall-through trap

`return` exits the function, so the version above needed no `break`. The moment a branch does
work instead of returning, a missing `break` runs **every following case too**.

// Your turn — retype the example above from memory, then run it.
// Typing beats reading. Peek above if you get stuck.

## Concept 3 - `throw`

`throw` stops the function immediately and hands an error to whoever called it. In a test, an
uncaught throw is a **failure with your message on it** - which is what you want when a caller
asks for a tab that does not exist.

| Instead of | Do |
|---|---|
| `return null` | `throw new Error("...")` |
| Silently doing nothing | throw, so the test fails where the mistake is |

// Your turn — retype the example above from memory, then run it.
// Typing beats reading. Peek above if you get stuck.

## Concept 4 - a union of string literals

A type can be *a specific list of strings*. Now a typo is a **compile error**, months before it
is a test failure.

```ts
type TabName = "Pay Bills" | "Add Payee" | "Statements";
```

| Passed | Result |
|---|---|
| `"Pay Bills"` | fine |
| `"Payy Bills"` | `error TS2345: Argument of type '"Payy Bills"' is not assignable...` |

The kernel strips types, so the cell below shows the *values*. The compiler is what enforces the
list - the same split you met with `abstract` in [week5/day3_1](/learn/w5/d3/p1).

// Your turn — retype the example above from memory, then run it.
// Typing beats reading. Peek above if you get stuck.

blocks.text:
# Week 6, Day 1.2 - A second app, and a component

Week 5 built page objects for the banking app. A pattern you can only apply to the app you
learned it on is not a pattern - so today you apply it to a **different** site, and meet the
piece week 5 only described: a **component**.

> **Follow this one in your own project.** These examples are run by the Playwright test runner, which the editor here does not provide. Copy them into your own checkout to run them.

## Step 1 - the app, and what it can and cannot do

[Zero Bank](http://zero.webappsecurity.com) is a deliberately weak demo bank. Probed live before
this lesson was written:

| Page | Reachable? |
|---|---|
| Home, Login, Search, Feedback, Online Banking | **yes**, over `http://` |
| `https://` anything | **no** - `ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH` |
| Anything under `/bank/` (account summary, transfers) | **no** - redirects to `/login.html` |

The site's own credentials are refused over HTTP, and its HTTPS port offers a cipher modern
Chromium removed. So its signed-in pages **cannot be automated at all** from a current browser -
diagnosed in [day2_2](/learn/w6/d2/p2). Today uses the five public pages, which are plenty for one
framework, and the banking app for the component.

## Step 2 - the base class, again

Identical in shape to `week5/generated/pages/BasePage.ts`. That is the lesson.

One addition worth noting: `goto()` prepends `http://zero.webappsecurity.com`. The HTTP-only
quirk is now a **one-line fact in one file** instead of a prefix every page repeats.
## Step 3 - two page classes

| Method | Why it is shaped that way |
|---|---|
| `searchFor(phrase)` | there is **no search button** on this page, so the only way to submit is `keyboard.press("Enter")` |
| the `waitForURL` inside it | results are a real navigation; without the wait the next line races it |
| `SearchResultsPage` with one field | a class with a single locator still earns its place - it is where "results are `<li><a>`" lives |

// Your turn — retype the example above from memory, then run it.
// Typing beats reading. Peek above if you get stuck.

## Step 4 - the problem a component solves

The banking dashboard has **12** tiles. Written as page-object methods that is
`clickOnPayBills()`, `clickOnAddPayee()`, `clickOnStatements()` ... twelve methods whose bodies
differ by one string.

| Approach | Methods | Cost of a 13th tab |
|---|---|---|
| One method per tab | 12 | a new method, and a new test for it |
| One method + `switch` | **1** | **one new `case`** |

Three things in that file worth stopping on:

- **`TabName` is a union**, so `clickOnTab("Payy Bills")` fails to compile.
- **`"Statements"` is scoped to `.card` first.** That label appears **twice** on this dashboard -
  a bare click is the strict-mode violation from [week5/day5_2](/learn/w5/d5/p2). The
  component decides once; no test has to know.
- **`default` throws.** Unreachable while the union is respected, and the safety net when the
  caller is untyped JavaScript.

## Step 5 - what the run proved

| Step | Claim |
|---|---|
| 2 | a search for `"bank"` yields **exactly 2** links |
| 5 | **12** tiles; `clickOnTab("Pay Bills")` lands on `/paymentDashboard` |
| 7 | `"Statements"` matches **2** elements and the component still clicks cleanly |
| 8 | an unknown tab **rejects with `unknown tab`** rather than hanging until timeout |

Step 8 is the one to remember: a bad locator times out after 30 seconds and tells you nothing
useful. A `throw` fails in milliseconds with the reason.

// Your turn — retype the example above from memory, then run it.
// Typing beats reading. Peek above if you get stuck.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | What happens |
|---|---|
| Forgetting `break` | every case below yours also runs - see [day1_1](/learn/w6/d1/p1) |
| `clickOnTab(tab: string)` | you lose the compile-time check; typos become timeouts |
| Putting `NavBar` in `pages/` | it is not a screen; the folder stops meaning anything |
| A `default` that returns quietly | the test carries on and fails somewhere unrelated |

**Next:** [Day 1.3 - Where these files live](/learn/w6/d1/p3)

# Week 6, Day 1.3 - Where these files live

Same classes, same `switch` - arranged so a stranger can find things.

## The folder split

```
week6/generated/
  zero/                  <- one app's pages
    BasePage.ts
    HomePage.ts
    SearchResultsPage.ts
    LoginPage.ts
    FeedbackPage.ts
  components/            <- things that sit ON TOP of pages
    NavBar.ts
```

The test for whether something is a component: **can it appear on more than one page?** A nav
bar, a header, a cookie banner, a data table - yes. A login form - no.

## Two apps, two folders

This repo now holds page objects for two different sites. They do not share a base class, and
should not:

| | `week5/generated/pages/` | `week6/generated/zero/` |
|---|---|---|
| App | banking app (HTTPS, real login) | Zero Bank (HTTP only) |
| `BasePage.goto` | a path against `baseURL` | prepends the full `http://` origin |
| Login | succeeds | refused - see [day2_2](/learn/w6/d2/p2) |

A shared base class would have to know both, which is how a base class becomes a junk drawer.
**One base per app** is the rule; the *pattern* is what is shared, not the code.
Thirty seconds versus zero, per typo, forever. That is the whole argument for the union.

## Reviewer's checklist

| Look for | Why |
|---|---|
| A locator string in a spec file | the abstraction has a hole - see [day2_2](/learn/w6/d2/p2) |
| `tab: string` on a dispatcher | the union was the point |
| A component in `pages/` | folders stop carrying meaning |
| A base class that knows about a specific screen | it is not a base class any more |
| Two apps sharing one `BasePage` | the origin/login differences leak into everything |

**Next:** [Day 1.4 - Practice](/learn/w6/d1/p4)

# Week 6, Day 1.4 - Practice

Add files under `week6/generated/` rather than editing the ones you were given, so the Day 1.2
cells keep running.
**Next:** [Day 2.1 - Prerequisites](/learn/w6/d2/p1)

problems.statement:
**The page you were told to derive**
The session set this as a live exercise: build `zero/LoginPage.ts` yourself before reading it.
Locators for username, password, submit, "remember me", and the error banner; one `login()`
method.

**Right when:** a spec signs in with wrong details and asserts the banner is visible - and your
class has no `expect` in it yet. Then compare with the real file in [day2_2](/learn/w6/d2/p2).

**An OnlineBankingPage**
`#onlineBankingMenu` leads to `/online-banking.html`. Write the class and reach it *through*
`HomePage`.

**Right when:** the spec never writes a URL or a CSS selector.

**Break the switch on purpose**
Copy `NavBar.ts`, delete the `break` from one case, and run Day 1.2's spec against your copy.

**Right when:** you can say which test broke, what it did instead, and why
[day1_1](/learn/w6/d1/p1) concept 2 predicted it.

**Add a tab**
Add `"Recharge"` to `TabName` and to the switch. Find its destination URL yourself by clicking
the tile.

**Right when:** `clickOnTab("Recharge")` passes, and you changed exactly two places.

**Widen the type, feel the loss**
Change `clickOnTab(tab: TabName)` to `tab: string`. Then call it with `"Payy Bills"` and run
`npx tsc --noEmit`.

**Right when:** the compiler is now silent, the test fails after a ~30s timeout, and you can
state what the union was buying.

**Rewrite it as a lookup**
Convert your `NavBar` copy to the `Record<TabName, RegExp>` form from
[day1_3](/learn/w6/d1/p3) - handling `"Statements"` however you must.

**Right when:** the Day 1.2 component tests pass unchanged against your version, and you have an
opinion on which file you would rather own.

**A second component**
The banking dashboard's tiles all sit in `.card` elements - three of them. Write a `Cards`
component exposing `count()` and `labelsIn(cardIndex)`.

**Right when:** it reports **3** cards and **12** labels in total, and it lives in
`components/`, not `zero/`.
